chapter: Recording with King Oliver and Clarence Williams
title: Using sidemen to identify his Oliver and Williams sessions
summary: Waters says if Cy St. Clair on bass is not on a date he was not there; he also names Cuffey, Ben Whitted and Happy Cauldwell, and says the dates were done while he worked at Small's Paradise.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: All right, well let's do it this way, let's take known record dates that King Oliver did in the New York area because that's where you recorded with him besides the Clarence Williams -
QRS, Long Island.
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82
PS: Now July 8th, 1927 for Vocalion he records a tune called "Aunt Jemima" with supposedly Red Allen present, but the music was not issued. You -

Wait a second, let me give you the names of some, then you compare it with that book. Here's the, here's some of the names I remember real well. The first session we had Cy St. La, Cy St. Clair on bass. And if Cy St. Clair isn't on those records then I wasn't there, because every record that I made with Clarence Williams, Cy St. Clair was on it because he was the one that got me the job.
Um hum.
Now that's one thing, huh, that's one thing. If Cy St. Clair isn't on bass on those records there, then I wasn't there.
Right.
See, because Cy St. Clair got me the job. And he was on all the records that I made, he's there before me and after me also. Now here's another guy, Cuffey on trombone.
Right. But I'm saying if you're not listed they may not be listed either, I can only go, there are some of these dates -
Yeah -
PS: where there are no names listed. So now Cyrus St. Clair is on King Oliver's record date June 11th, 1928 [ ] for Vocalion.
PS: "Tin Roof Blues", "West End Blues", "Sweet Emalina" and "Lazy Mama". But the reeds listed are Arville Harris and Ernest Elliott.
Yeah.
Uh huh.
Well, Arville Harris made some. And then we had another -
Omer Simeon?
No, not, I didn't never make any with him.
Paul Barnes?
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82
That could have, Paul Barnes could have.
Um hum. Do you remember making the 'Tin Roof Blues?'
No, I can't, I don't remember the songs I've been on, the only thing, the only song I can remember is 'Snag It'.
Uh huh.
But it might not - the first thing, the sessions that I made mostly, were not for Vocation. The most of 'em that I made was in QRS in Long Island.
Well, those were the Clarence Williams sides.
No, Joe Oliver was -
Joe Oliver was the sideman, but the record date's under King Oliver's name.

Yeah, but they, that's what's confusing with people, lot of times it was King. Clarence Williams' band, and Joe was playin' trumpet. Then another time it was Joe Oliver's band and Clarence Williams playin' piano. You see what I mean?
Right.
That's where the confusion comes in.
Now there -

Look, they, the first thing they worked together, that's the first thing, they worked together, they had a music company down there. Clarence Williams had the music company, and Joe was workin' right there because all he sold were him, Clarence Williams Orchestra before he sold it. See, that's where I came in.
Um hum.
That;'s where the confusing part, where people don't understand, say Clarence Williams - I mean Joe was there, too.
Did you make any of the Victor sessions with King Oliver?
No, I don't remember making any Victor. Only Victor sessions I made was Charlie Johnson.
And did you record, did you work with King Oliver or just made record dates?
No, only record dates. I was workin' with Charlie Johnson's band, see what I'm
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82

talking about? [ ], I was workin' with Charlie Johnson's band at Small's Paradise when I did all the recording. You see, like I was saying - I was recommended by Cy St. Clair, and Cy St. Clair was workin' with me every night. See what I mean, that's who recommended me, see, so - if Cy St. Clair wasn't there on those records you have, then I wasn't there, you see? You have to have, if Cy St. Clair was there before me and made every session with me on tuba - so I don't know, I mean, if you don't have Cy St. Clair there, -
Well -
then -
Well -
then, well you wouldn't have me because -

Well just say that any King Oliver session or any session that King Oliver appears on within the confines of his New York period in the late '20's should be re-examined in the context that you might be there, simple as that.
No, no, no, all you say - yeah, or say, be sure the the sides say Clair was there because he recommended me to -
Yeah, I was sayin', but it's hard to, if you -
And Ben Whitted -
don't have any names.
And Ben Whitted also made some, he's - do you find his name there?
Ben Whitted, by the way, his name was W-H-I -
I-T-T-E-D, yeah.
They always have that wrong.

Well, he stayed, he was on it, he was on it before me, because it was Cy St. Clair that brought Ben Whitted in. And when I got sick Happy Cauldwell took my place on some of them. See, so that was the names that you must have. You don't have those names - if you don't have Cy St. Clair, then I wasn't on it at all. Or something wrong with the, you know. See, 'cause that's who recommend me, you know. Say, I didn't make nothing without him bein' there because everybody was saying how great he was, he was a great bass player. But he was working with Charlie Johnson's band before he ever recorded with, so you see. 'Cause he's the one the got the job recording, then he brought, you know how those guys are kind of clique-dy, you know.
